newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds set for Greenspan Mark II.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds set for Greenspan Mark II.

text.p: *A late squeeze saw Australian bond yields close around the day's lows, but overall domestic institutions were seen going into U.S. Humphrey-Hawkins testimony short on balance.

A late squeeze saw Australian bond saw yields close around the day's lows, but overall domestic institutions were seen remaining short on balance going into the second-leg of the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent shock-waves globally after his hawkish comments last week when he warned of a pre-emptive tightening in U.S. monetary policy and felt that the stock market had risen too far because of "investors exuberance."
Locally, the fourth quarter national account proved a non-event, coming much in line with expectations.

"The figures today were pretty much historical and that's very much how they were regarded. This quarter is what's more important and growth seems to have picked up," said Chris Bell, Director of Treasury at Dresdner Bank.

Fourth quarter GDP rose 0.5 percent, much in line with the partial indicators seen in recent weeks, although the annual rate was smaller than forecast at 3.1 percent, reflecting revisions to previous quarters.
However, recent data, such as Tuesday's rebound in retail trade and sharp jump in building approvals, suggest that the economy has got over its soft patch.

Bond yields have risen sharply in the past few weeks as all hopes of a monetary policy easing have been squeezed out of the market amid a more robust economic outlook, touching their highest level of the year on Tuesday.

However, there is a general feeling that the move in yields has been overdone given the current benign outlook for inflation, and buyers are returning, particularly from offshore, with the market now seen more attractively priced, traders said.
U.S. Treasury yields, meanwhile, were modestly lower in Tokyo after rising in a nervous New York session ahead of Greenspan's testimony.

The local market made a strong outperformance against its dollar bloc partners, ending the recent widening trend of the past few weeks. The U.S. weakness filtered through to the Canadian market, while New Zealand debt has turned bearish ahead of next week's RBNZ economic forecasts.
